stem: A vomiting child has abdominal pain and guarding; which diagnosis is the clearest medical exception to the rule that medical causes should not produce guarding or rigidity?
explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is the key medical exception that can present with abdominal pain and guarding or rigidity, so it can mimic a surgical abdomen.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because pneumonia may cause referred abdominal pain, but it is not the recognised exception to the guarding or rigidity rule.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because constipation can cause abdominal pain, but it is not the specific medical exception described here.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because DKA is the notable medical cause that can present with abdominal pain and guarding or rigidity, making it an exception to the usual rule.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because psychosocial stress may contribute to symptoms, but it does not explain guarding or rigidity as the named exception.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because urinary symptoms may point towards a urinary tract cause, but they are not the specific exception to the guarding or rigidity rule.
